title: Sync and fulfillment resilience: data-integrity and retry-safety hardening

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every terminal lifecycle command persists order state, immutable source evidence, exact fulfillment-line claims, package work, and inventory-deduction intent in one backend-owned transaction; forced rollback plus retry cannot leave partial state or duplicate work.

Shipment, label, sync, import, webhook, manual, and marketplace callers provide shipment-scoped exact fulfillment facts or an explicit review-only unavailable result; mutable whole-order quantities never create inventory intent, and repeat settlement is a no-op.

Shopify and direct label purchase use durable fail-closed intent plus an immutable backend quote authorization bound to the exact order, tenant, credential account, environment, package, service, addresses, and purchase facts; mismatches reject before the provider, and acknowledged or ambiguous operations cannot create a second purchase.

ShipStation confirmation retry re-reads upstream shipped truth, uses the durable provider-operation ledger for one-effect fencing and reconciliation, and leaves the marketplace notification spy at one call after simulated local-settlement loss.

Inventory recovery remains ledger-idempotent and kill-switch governed; the bounded recent production dry-run reported 672 of 672 shipped lines and 881 of 881 units represented, with zero missing orders and no apply.

The nine production provider-pending health facts are safely classified read-only: all nine have durable provider receipts on active outbound shipments, across eight orders and three inactive jobs, and unresolved label-purchase-intent count is zero.

The focused PS-422 quote-authorization, PS-423 provider-operation, PS-424 lifecycle, PS-426 worker-leadership, and PS-432 resilience suites, all 45 mandatory source-of-truth guards, runtime-schema readiness audit, strict TypeScript checks, and production frontend build pass at the exact reviewed SHA; later Billing and customer-shipping-money changes were classified as independent backend owners.

Shipped/cancelled protections and the inventory kill switch are not weakened; closure performs no production write, label purchase or void, postage charge, marketplace notification, inventory movement, or automatic retry.

Exactly one worker owns the ShipStation stately consumers; active-job handoff, PostgreSQL connection loss, fallback ping detection, retry cancellation, and idempotent shutdown reacquire or release leadership without concurrent provider work.

sotBypass.details: Terminal lifecycle truth, exact fulfillment facts, inventory movement, quote authorization, purchase intent, provider-operation reconciliation, confirmation settlement, provider notification idempotency, and worker leadership remain in named backend owners. Routes, adapters, and the frontend transport or display backend-issued intent only and own none of these decisions.

evidence.proves: The additive 0070 schema and canonical lifecycle command run against a migrated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture. Two shipments claim only their exact quantities; Shopify partial fulfillment uses fulfillment-order quantities rather than mutable order totals; void-before-deduction, void-after-deduction, changed-quantity relabel, concurrent retries, stale writers, and injected transaction rollback preserve one append-only receipt and no duplicate inventory or package effect. Explicitly unavailable facts create review-only lifecycle evidence and no inventory outbox.

Provider-free behavioral proof covers two-worker exclusion, active-job handoff, immediate PostgreSQL onclose ownership loss, fallback ping loss detection and reacquisition ordering, retry/timer cancellation, and idempotent shutdown. One hundred foreground admission samples stayed below 500 ms with zero database connections and zero provider calls.

Real canonical owners execute against a current-schema PostgreSQL-compatible fixture: rollback removes both status and intent, retry commits one pair, concurrent duplicate intents retain one durable row, torn confirmation projections reconverge once, and repeat operations have no second effect.

A Shopify retry is blocked before a second purchase-spy call; cross-order shipment proof and no-label proof conflicting with an active shipment are rejected; a stale terminal resolver is rejected; and ShipStation retry keeps marketplace notifications at one.

Injected transaction failure, provider-ACK/local-persistence loss, torn succeeded projection, and confirmation-ACK/local-settlement loss recover without missing intent, duplicate purchase, duplicate notification, or stale overwrite.

evidence.proves: Production read-only classification reports nine stale sidecar facts, nine durable shipment/provider receipts, eight distinct orders, three inactive jobs, six queue entries, and zero unresolved purchase intents. No provider or write boundary was touched.

The current backend quote authorization rejects order, client/store, credential, environment, origin, destination, package, service, weight, dimensions, residential, confirmation, insurance, and identity mismatches before the provider spy. Direct label and Print Queue callers consume the same opaque selectionRef and cannot reconstruct purchase authority.

The additive provider-operation ledger runs against a migrated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture with fake providers only. Concurrent reservation, lease loss, acknowledged-provider/local-persistence loss, unknown outcome, restart, and repeat reconciliation preserve one external effect and one durable receipt.

The recorded bounded production dry-run found no missing recent ledger lines/orders, while the tool defaults to dry-run and refuses unbounded --all --apply; the inventory kill switch and ledger idempotency owner remain intact.

migrations.rollbackPlan: If a PS-432 runtime regression is found, prepare a reviewed forward revert of the original PS-432/PS-424/PS-426 runtime commits while leaving additive lifecycle and provider-operation receipt tables intact. Preserve later independent Billing/PS-437 work and the PS-422/PS-423 safety owners unless their own reviewed rollback is separately approved; never drop append-only evidence or rewrite historical shipped/cancelled meaning.

rollback.strategy: Use a reviewed forward revert of the original PS-432/PS-424/PS-426 runtime changes only; do not reset the branch or roll back later independent Billing/PS-437 work or the PS-422/PS-423 safety owners. Keep additive 0070, 0071, and 0072 sidecars and durable receipts; never delete lifecycle, provider-operation, shipment, intent, outbox, inventory-ledger, package-ledger, or billing history and never mutate shipped/cancelled production records. The integration's injected exception proves the authoritative transaction rolls back all new lifecycle writes before a safe retry.

caveats.description: Nine historical Print Queue sidecar states remain conservatively visible to deep health, but read-only canonical shipment evidence classifies all nine provider outcomes as already durably successful.
